answer: Oceanic Sybil attacks can be mitigated by deploying a beacon-based reputation system. Agents must stake assets in a verifiable delay function to authorize claims, incurring substantial capital lockup. An attacker attempting to create numerous sybils would suffer negative expected utility due to the economic cost, akin to navigating the nebula without a guiding light. This mechanism ensures Byzantine fault tolerance across autonomous agents by maintaining trust through stake-slashing matrices and zero-knowledge reputation commitments.
